purpose: Task 0 extraction and current-semantics audit only. No API output has been classified by this task.

referenceLike.predicate: type.kind == Array OR (not Named System.Void AND GetTypeRecord(type)?.shape == Reference)
referenceLike.getTypeRecord: Named -> runtimeName; ConstructedGeneric -> definition.runtimeName; everything else -> no record. Exact lookup in physicalModel.TypesByRuntimeName, including unexposed records.
referenceLike.primitive: No primitive-name heuristic. System.String/System.Object are reference-like if their records say Reference; numeric/bool/char records say Value and are Raw.
referenceLike.valueAndEnum: Value/Enum records are Raw, including reference-bearing structs; no recursive field inspection.
referenceLike.array: Array is reference-like regardless of element. Projection wraps the entire array, not each element. Array has no GetTypeRecord result: neither System.Array nor an element type exception exempts Array. UnsupportedArray is not Array and is Raw here; catalog rank != 1 becomes UnsupportedArray.
referenceLike.unityObject: UnityEngine.Object and subclasses use the same Reference shape rule. No special handling of destroyed objects, overloaded ==, native liveness, or Unity truthiness.
referenceLike.generic: ConstructedGeneric uses the generic definition record, independent of arguments. GenericParameter itself is Raw even with reference constraints; no substitution/constraint-based nullability analysis occurs in policy. A generic definition type rule applies across all constructed instantiations encountered by policy.
referenceLike.unknown: Unresolved record, null/invalid TypeRef and unrecognized kind are not reference-like; Raw here is NOT evidence of a non-null contract.

order: Load config v5 and normalize; validate duplicate/invalid configuration; project catalog v2 into physical member surfaces including inherited members.
Create type exclusions; ApplyMemberPolicy returns early for excluded physical owners or member ClrSignature. Those outputs never reach Maybe rule matching.
Set return projection: constructor/property setter/field setter -> Raw; otherwise reference-like -> GetDefaultProjection; all other return types -> Raw.
GetDefaultProjection: non-reference-like -> Raw; exact output type-record runtimeName in nonMaybeTypes -> Raw and mark rule matched; otherwise Maybe.
For non-write surfaces, exact ClrSignature in nonMaybeReturns -> mark matched; require reference-like non-constructor return or error; set Raw. This may be redundant with a type exception.

If the resulting return is Maybe and any parameter passingMode is Ref or Out, fail the whole policy with an error. This happens BEFORE out exceptions; no evidence-free override may be used to bypass it.
For each Out parameter independently, apply GetDefaultProjection. Ref/In/Value parameters do not get Maybe projections.
Match nonMaybeOuts.member by exact ClrSignature; for every listed parameter NAME find the first exact ordinal-name match, require Out and reference-like or error; set that position Raw.
If the physical member was otherwise generated, mark indexed properties and params parameters unsupported. Additional operator-host relocation/duplicate/static-module skips occur in Apply.

Reject stale rules with no matches; Maybe rules do not reject multiple physical matches. Downstream generator ambiguity, supported-declaration, binder-validation and duplicate-declaration passes may still reject policy-eligible members. This audit never calls Generate.
currentImplementation.return: Includes methods, operators, property getters and field getters. Ordinary constructor results are always Raw; setters have Void return. No accessor-name inference.
currentImplementation.out: A zero-based index refers to the entire physical parameter list, not just out parameters or Sobakasu inputs. Each Out is a separate candidate; config addresses it by original physical parameter name, not index. Ref is returned by adapter formatting but remains Raw and is outside Maybe exception scope.
currentImplementation.renderer: Consumes projections already stored in generated models. Return type formatting wraps Maybe<type>; extern out declarations use maybe out; adapter result ordering is ordinary non-Void return first, then Ref/Out positions in parameter order, with tuples for multiple outputs. Inputs and array elements are not recursively projected.
currentImplementation.noPositiveOverride: No rule can restore Maybe for one output after a nonMaybeTypes exception. All three exception kinds only move outputs toward Raw.

nonMaybeTypes.match: Ordinal exact equality to output record.runtimeName, NOT physical host, declaring type, inheritance subtree, formatted Sobakasu type, or arbitrary CLR type pattern.
nonMaybeTypes.scope: All reference-like return/Out positions that reach GetDefaultProjection and resolve to that record, across members/hosts/namespaces. No array exemption and no Ref projection. Constructed generic arguments are not distinguished.
nonMaybeTypes.tracking: Type candidate affectedOutputIds lists the complete extracted output group. Members excluded before projection are retained with policyEligible false; the rule cannot currently change them. No rule exists for unused reference records because it would be stale.

nonMaybeReturns.match: Ordinal exact equality to physical.ClrSignature, treated as opaque. Current persisted catalog loader formats declarations as owner.method(parameterTypes), owner for constructors, or owner.member for all accessors; nested '+' becomes '.' in this signature.
nonMaybeReturns.scope: Every non-write physical surface with that ClrSignature. Inherited surfaces retain declaring-member ClrSignature, so one rule can affect many physical hosts. No per-host narrowing is available.

nonMaybeOuts.match: member is ordinal exact physical.ClrSignature; parameters are ordinal exact original parameter names. One rule per member is allowed; multiple out names belong in its parameters array.
nonMaybeOuts.scope: Every physical surface with the matched signature; each listed name must identify an Out reference-like parameter on every reached surface. Cannot address an index directly. Duplicate/empty names, no names, missing parameter, non-Out parameter and non-reference type are errors.

selectorCapabilities.physicalHost: Not independently selectable for inherited members; ClrSignature owner is declaration owner.
selectorCapabilities.memberKind: Not explicitly encoded; method/property/field kinds have no structured discriminator. Getter/setter share signature.
selectorCapabilities.parameterType: Methods encode formatted parameter types and positions; accessor signatures discard index parameters.
selectorCapabilities.passingMode: Ref/Out/In all become '&'; these modes cannot be distinguished by Maybe member strings.
selectorCapabilities.genericArity: Not explicitly encoded; generic parameter placeholders may distinguish some shapes but not all arities.
selectorCapabilities.overload: Ordinary method parameter-type overloads can be distinguished; not a complete physical identity.
selectorCapabilities.accessor: Cannot select getter/setter independently by string; return processing ignores setters so a shared getter/setter string does not itself modify a setter return. Field/property getter collisions or differing indexers may still be unsafe.
selectorCapabilities.outPosition: Only through parameter name under a member string, no integer position in schema.
selectorCapabilities.ambiguity: Only receivers.readonly uses structured selector equality and count>1 rejection. Maybe rule match counts check zero/stale, NOT ambiguity. Duplicate rule entries are rejected. See selector-collisions.json for collisions and selector-match-groups.json for all relevant current physical matches.

configRules.candidateSelectorRepresentation: candidate.selector is the ACTUAL current Maybe config entry (string or {member,parameters}). candidate.physicalIdentity is audit metadata derived from the existing structured member identity (host/member, kind, static state, parameter TypeRefs/passing, generic arity); it is NOT a proposed Maybe schema. Static/constructor identities are not valid readonly config entries. All physical identity match counts are checked using production UdonBindingMemberSelector equality, not display strings.

classification.non-null: Positive evidence establishes that the output cannot be null on ANY normal return within the stated target environment, across all legal input/state paths in scope. An exception/abort is not a normal return. API naming and current Raw projection are never evidence.
classification.nullable: Evidence establishes a contract or reachable normal-return path yielding null, without restricting the assessment to an unsupported success-only correlation. State the null-producing path.
classification.conditional: The non-null guarantee depends on a stated condition such as bool success, another out value, an argument/state condition, or success/failure branch. Record both sides and any known null-producing path. When both nullable-path evidence and an explicit correlated guarantee exist, use conditional as the primary classification and record nullable behavior in evidence.
classification.uncertain: Evidence is insufficient, environment-mismatched, contradictory, or stops at an unresolved boundary; neither non-null nor nullable can safely be established.
classification.retentionRule: nullable, conditional and uncertain retain Maybe. Current Generator rules cannot express boolean/out/argument correlations. Only reviewed non-null assessments are potential exceptions, never automatic config edits.
classification.typeRule: Assess the whole exact rule scope, not a CLR type's ability to exist. Read affectedOutputIds across all shards. A type rule requires affirmative non-null evidence for EVERY affected output and all applicable generic instantiations; one nullable/conditional/uncertain position blocks approval. Record uncovered outputs and generic-scope limits. The type-wide scope also applies to future matching outputs, which needs explicit review.
classification.unityNull: Record separately CLR null, UnityEngine.Object overloaded-null/destroyed state, and native liveness. Current policy only classifies shapes. Do not equate these notions or infer non-null from Unity truthiness; assess the actual extern/Maybe null-test path if relevant.

requiredContext: Exact candidate ID and output position
Target Unity/SDK versions and platform/runtime scope
Source URL or repository file+line and version/hash
Normal-return path coverage and argument/state preconditions

kinds.explicit-api-contract: Direct output-specific guarantee or explicit nullable/conditional contract, matched to the actual version and environment. Preserve exact scope and short quotation or precise source location.
kinds.nullability-annotation-metadata: Inspect annotation encoding, nullable context, attributes (including conditional annotations) and build/version. Missing annotations are unknown. Non-null annotation is evidence, not unquestionable runtime proof; conflicts or a weaker managed/native path require resolution.
kinds.managed-implementation: Use the assembly actually distributed for the target Unity/SDK; record path, SHA-256, assembly identity and member token/signature. Official matching source may assist; .NET 8 host runtime is not substitute evidence for Unity Mono/BCL.
kinds.il-control-flow-analysis: Enumerate all reachable normal return paths, branches, local merges, exception handlers/finally, field loads and returned values; distinguish reachability assumptions. Allocation proves only that allocated value; storing/returning a callee result or field requires further evidence.
kinds.managed-callee-analysis: Follow every returned value through all relevant managed callees; resolve virtual/interface dispatch or list possible targets. Record visited callees and evidence. Unresolved dispatch is a boundary, not a non-null proof.
kinds.native-boundary: P/Invoke, internalcall, Unity native bindings and engine externs require a matching explicit contract or authoritative native/source evidence. A managed wrapper returning a native value does not establish non-null.
kinds.external-indirect-call: Delegates, callbacks, reflection, network/service responses and unknown assemblies require evidence for all relevant targets or explicit contracts; otherwise uncertain or conditional.
kinds.official-documentation: Version-specific official documentation is admissible when it explicitly covers nullability of this output/path; silence is no guarantee. Record edition/version/date and direct URL.
kinds.source-code: Pin repository/version/path/lines and demonstrate correspondence to the distributed artifact. Reference source or a different engine/runtime release alone cannot establish this target's contract.
kinds.inference-only: May guide searches or explain a hypothesis; never sufficient for non-null, nullable or conditional without corroborating output-specific evidence.

forbiddenInference: Array results usually use empty arrays
General API naming or design conventions
One observed successful execution proves every path
evidencePolicy.conflictPolicy: Document conflicts; use uncertain unless target-specific evidence resolves them. Do not silently choose the stronger guarantee.
evidencePolicy.assemblyPolicy: Task 0 used no managed assembly as API contract evidence. Workers must locate actual shipped Unity 2022.3.22f1 / SDK 3.10.4 assemblies before managed/IL/callee analysis, pin hashes, and distinguish Editor-only, client/runtime and platform variants. Do not silently substitute another installed version.

workerProtocol.ownership: One assigned Worker per candidate ID; repeated CLR declarations on different physical hosts remain separate outputs. Share evidence by declaration when justified but preserve host/ABI checks and output IDs.
workerProtocol.configReview: No Worker may add config entries from this extraction. Any future proposal must cover every physicalTargetIds entry in the candidate configMatchGroupId (selector-match-groups.json) and check errors on all matches, not merely one reviewed candidate. Candidate-level non-null is insufficient for a colliding string or broad type rule.
workerProtocol.sharding: Sort by deterministic SHA-256 candidate ID using ordinal ordering, then assign index modulo five to A..E. Type-rule dependencies can span shards; affectedOutputIds is authoritative.

extraction.source: Persisted catalog v2 loaded through production UdonBindingSourceModel.Load; production UdonBindingGenerationPolicy.Apply is executed read-only. No binding/library generation is invoked.
extraction.filter: Every projected physical member's reference-like return except constructor/write surface, plus every reference-like Out parameter position, even when policy-skipped. One type candidate per exact output record runtimeName reachable from these positions, plus every existing type rule.
extraction.exclusions: Non-reference outputs, constructor ordinary returns, write surfaces and Ref projections appear in excluded-output-positions.json. Unmodeled ABI signatures and array capabilities are explicitly listed in special-cases.json; no physical output model exists for them in this policy. Unexposed declarations are not projected as callable candidates.
extraction.identity: physical ID = SHA256(canonical JSON of structured identity, return TypeRef, declaring runtime name, extern signature). Output ID = SHA256(canonical JSON of rule kind, physical ID, zero-based parameter index). Type ID = SHA256(canonical JSON of rule kind and exact record runtimeName). Full hexadecimal hashes; JSON keys sorted, UTF-8, compact separators; no timestamp/path/config classification in ID.
extraction.completenessClaim: Complete for the stated filter over the persisted projected physical model, NOT a mathematical enumeration of all Udon APIs, all runtime platforms, or all signatures in the catalog. Source counts, hashes, special cases, mappings and assertions make the scope reproducible.
extraction.eligibility: policyEligible records only policy-stage type/member skips. Downstream generator passes and actual emitted-library membership were not executed or inferred. Excluded candidates must not be assumed config-applicable.
